headline: President Bush changes Executive Order 12866, the order that sets how federal agencies plan regulations and how the White House reviews them.
what_it_does: This order amends Executive Order 12866, which sets the steps federal agencies follow when they plan and write new regulations, including review by the White House. No summary was provided, so the specific changes are not described here. Changes to this order usually affect who inside the executive branch oversees regulatory review, not the rules themselves.

who_it_affects.how: They may have to follow a changed process or report to different officials when planning and submitting rules for review.

who_it_affects.group: White House officials who review regulations
who_it_affects.how: Their roles or duties in reviewing agency rules may be changed.

when_it_takes_effect: 2002-02-26 (date signed; actual effective date not stated in the source)
